statewideTerm: Puerto Rico's governor and legislature were elected in November 2024 for four-year terms (2025-2028); there was no territorial election in 2026. The Secretary of State and the Secretary of Justice (its attorney general) are appointed by the governor and confirmed by the Senate. Puerto Rico has no U.S. senators; it elects one non-voting Resident Commissioner to the House.

notes.election: Puerto Rico's governor, Legislative Assembly and Resident Commissioner serve terms that began in January 2025; the next territorial election is in November 2028, so this list is current. Puerto Rico has no U.S. senators; it elects one non-voting Resident Commissioner to the House. Members elected at large ("por acumulación") represent everyone in the territory and are listed with each district.
